# hands/surplus

Teeny's spare SOL, swept to the surplus wallet as USDC on Base.

## Not available to you

The exec fence refuses `hands/surplus` to you: a call is blocked before it runs. Its jobs and the operator run it. Do not try it, and do not look for another way to do what it would do. What follows is for reference only.

## How it is called (reference)

The operator and the jobs invoke it from the repository root as `hands/surplus <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): none
- Job (writes state or calls the core): sweep
- Operator only (never call): none
- Read only: status; log [--max N]

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `sweep` | J | Pays USDC on Base above the reserve to the surplus wallet, then bridges SOL above its reserve straight into USDC on Base at the surplus wallet. |
| `status` | R | The settings, what went to the surplus wallet in the last 7 days and in all, the last five runs. |
| `log [--max N]` | R | The runs (`surplus_runs`), newest first. |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `log`, `status`, `sweep`.

Flags named in the hand's source: `--max`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `hands/surplus <verb> --help` (never put a VAR= in front of a command: the shell refuses it, and DRY_RUN is not yours to set). The full account is in docs/hands.md.
